title: SharePoint: find information and get answers from Lists in Knowledge Agent
summary: The briefing passes: the control paths, commands, default and licensing are supported by Microsoft documentation. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap's overdue targets from the broader Copilot in SharePoint rollout and marks the old PowerShell availability controls as historical.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery availability restrictions still apply to Copilot in SharePoint regardless of other settings.
claims.quote: If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change permissions or prevent authorized users accessing content directly.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: SharePoint site pages and lists do not inherit their container's sensitivity label.

claims.claim: SharePoint site pages and lists do not display their container's sensitivity label in Copilot.
claims.quote: Similarly, content from SharePoint site pages and lists won't display the sensitivity label of their container label.

claims.claim: The site-level Site AI panel opens through Settings > Site AI.
claims.quote: To open the panel, go to **Settings** > **Site AI**.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes Copilot and AI-action entry points from selected sites and limits Copilot discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery also removes AI-powered entry points from these SharePoint sites. Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or **Create pages with AI**.

claims.claim: The organization must be licensed for Copilot to configure Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: SharePoint Advanced Management must be available to configure Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: A separate tenant setting delegates Restricted Content Discovery management to site administrators.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $true
When delegation is enabled, site administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery for their sites.

claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path is Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Sites** and select **Active sites**. Select the site you want to configure. Open the **Settings** tab, and then turn **Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot** on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -KnowledgeAgentScope NoSites is the documented historical command disabling preview availability across the tenant.
claims.quote:
Turn off Copilot in SharePoint for the tenant
Set-SPOTenant -KnowledgeAgentScope NoSites

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the historical tenant-wide KnowledgeAgentScope preview control.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint KnowledgeAgentScope preview availability admin center UI tenant opt out. Read get-started availability, PowerShell details and examples; search excerpts document Site AI and unrelated Power Platform controls, not a UI for KnowledgeAgentScope.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; Governance controls; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Advanced work, including work at greater scale, uses usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits rather than the included everyday entitlement.
claims.quote: Everyday individual productivity is included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Advanced work requires usage-based billing enabled through a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To use advanced capabilities or to work at greater scale, users need usage-based billing enabled through a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center and available Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Copilot asks the user to approve credit use before continuing into advanced work.
claims.quote: When a prompt requires an advanced capability, or crosses the threshold of working at scale, Copilot asks the user to approve credit use before continuing.

claims.claim: The spending-policy path is Copilot > Cost management > Add spending policy > Access scope > Agents and services > Advanced work in SharePoint > Limits and alerts.
claims.quote: go to **Copilot** > **Cost management**. Select **Add spending policy** ... Under **Access scope** ... Under **Agents and services**, select **Advanced work in SharePoint**. Set **Limits and alerts** for the policy

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates a spending policy's limits through the beta Graph API.
periodLimit is an updatable request-body property for the beta spending-policy operation.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `billingMethods`.

claims.claim: perUserLimit is an updatable request-body property for the beta spending-policy operation.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `billingMethods`.

claims.claim: Copilot warns users when 20% of their monthly credit limit remains.
claims.quote: When 20% of the monthly credit limit remains, Copilot notifies the user that usage-based features pause until the next month when the limit is reached.

claims.claim: The SharePoint page says usage-based features pause until the next month at the credit limit, with the running-task exception reported separately.
claims.quote: Copilot notifies the user that usage-based features pause until the next month when the limit is reached. Users can request more credits from that prompt.

claims.claim: A running task exceeding a group spending policy's per-user limit can complete without interruption.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.claim: Existing spending policies might automatically include new services if Allow new agents and services as they become available is enabled.
claims.quote: Existing cost management policies might automatically include newly available services if the **Allow new agents and services as they become available** option is turned on for the policy.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the **Users** > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select **Licenses and Apps**. Expand the **Licenses** section

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence to a user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.
